# The data worker's webpackInclude is unanchored, so a workspace nested under an 'apps' ancestor bundles its whole tree

`src/worker/Data.mjs#createInstance` narrows its dynamic import with a `webpackInclude` magic comment:

```js
let module = await import(
    /* webpackInclude: /(?:apps|docs\/app|examples|src\/data)\/.*\.mjs$/ */
    /* webpackExclude: /(?:\/|\\)(buildScripts|dist|node_modules(?:\/|\\)(?!neo\.mjs)|ai(?:\/|\\)|\.claude(?:\/|\\)|server\.mjs|test(?:\/|\\))/ */
    /* webpackMode: "lazy" */
    `../../${path}.mjs`
);
```

The context base is the repository root, and the include is what keeps that from meaning "every
`.mjs` in the tree". **It is unanchored, and webpack matches include/exclude against the absolute
resource path** — so any workspace with an ancestor directory named `apps`, `examples`, or `docs/app`
matches on the ancestor, and the include stops narrowing anything.

The exclude on the very next line *is* separator-anchored (`(?:\/|\\)(buildScripts|…)`), so the
anchoring question was clearly considered for one of the two and not the other.

## Measured, with a control

Same engine version (13.1.0), same config, two `dist/development/dataworker.js` builds:

| build | context map entries | entries matching the include **relative to the root** |
|---|---|---|
| this repo — no ancestor named `apps` | 797 | **762** (95.6%) |
| a workspace nested under a parent directory named `apps` | 1244 | **7** (0.6%) |

In this repo the include works, because the `apps/` it matches *is* the one at the context root. That
is why the defect is invisible here and why it survived: the pattern is correct exactly when the
repository is the thing being built.

In the nested workspace 1237 of 1244 registered modules match no relative form of the include. Files
that reach the bundle include root-level Node-only scripts — a `bootstrap.mjs` and a `devServer.mjs`,
each dragging a `node_modules/url` vendor chunk — and unrelated application trees such as
`client/src/**`. A dev server is registered as a lazily-importable module inside a browser Web
Worker.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

- **It is silent.** The build succeeds, the app runs, and the only symptom is bundle size plus code
  that could never execute in a worker being reachable from one.
- **It is invisible to this repo's own builds**, so no amount of testing here surfaces it.
- **The trigger is the consumer's directory name**, not anything the consumer wrote. Nesting a
  workspace under `apps/` is an ordinary layout choice, and nothing reports that it changed the build.

## The shape of the fix

Filtering a too-wide context with a pattern is the fragile part; the pattern has to encode "relative
to the context root" in a language that only sees absolute paths. Making the **context base explicit**
avoids the class rather than tightening the regex — e.g. separate narrow imports per supported root
(`../../apps/…`, `../../examples/…`, `../../src/data/…`) selected from the already-parsed `path`, so
each context is rooted where it should be and an ancestor's name cannot widen it.

Tightening the include to require a separator (`(?:\/|\\)(?:apps|…)`) is **not** sufficient: an
ancestor path still supplies the separator.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

Backfilled 2026-08-30 at @neo-gpt's RA-3. The ticket originally prescribed one layer; the defect
spans two, and the ledger has to say which layer owns what or the next change repeats the mistake.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `createInstance({config, path})` | `src/worker/Data.mjs` | consumed RMA method. Accepted roots: `apps/`, `examples/`, `docs/app/`, `src/data/`. A trailing `.mjs` suffix is stripped before dispatch, so `apps/x/M` and `apps/x/M.mjs` name the same module | unsupported root throws, and is never resolved through a wider context | method JSDoc | unit suite; physical consumer build |
| `loadModule({path})` | `src/worker/Data.mjs` | consumed RMA method; same four roots, same suffix rule, same refusal, via the shared helper | as above | method JSDoc | as above |
| `importAppSpaceModule(path)` | `src/worker/Data.mjs` | one static-prefixed lazy context per root. **Package-relative only** — this layer never decides what `apps/` means on disk | typed refusal: `Unsupported module root: <path>` | method JSDoc, which names the config-side half | in-repo 930-chunk identity |
| `workerContextRebasePlugin(insideNeo)` | `buildScripts/webpack/workerContextRebasePlugin.mjs` | **ownership boundary.** App-space roots (`apps`, `examples`, `docs/app`) resolve to the *consumer workspace*; `src/data` stays *package-local*. An absent optional root keeps its package-relative request with an emptied match, so it contributes no modules and raises no resolution error | `insideNeo` is a total no-op — the framework's own build is unaffected | factory JSDoc | 0 request mutations at `insideNeo=true` |
| development / dist parity | both `buildScripts/webpack/{development,production}/webpack.config.worker.mjs` | both modes install the same factory, so the mapping cannot differ between a dev build and a shipped one | none — divergence is the defect this row exists to prevent | workflow comment | consumer fixture built in both modes |

**The invariant the two layers share:** `Data.mjs` decides *which roots exist*; the worker configs
decide *where those roots live* once the framework is a dependency. Changing the prefixes in one
without the other breaks module resolution for every consumer, and the framework's own build cannot
observe it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The data worker's lazy context is rooted at the intended directories, so an ancestor directory
      named `apps`, `examples`, or `docs/app` cannot widen it.
- [ ] A build produced from a workspace nested under such an ancestor registers only modules under
      the supported roots — proven by counting map entries against the intended set, since the build
      succeeds either way and the count is the only signal.
- [ ] This repo's own build is unchanged: `createInstance` still resolves the same modules it does
      today.
- [ ] Root-level Node-only scripts in a consuming workspace are not registered in a worker bundle.

## Out of Scope

- The identical `webpackInclude`/`webpackExclude` pairs elsewhere in `src/worker/Data.mjs` and
  `src/worker/App.mjs` — same class, but each needs its own before/after count rather than being
  swept along on the strength of this one.
